sources.title: Fulltone 69 Pedal mkII | AllThePedals
sources.description: The Fulltone '69 mkII is a fuzz pedal designed to emulate the fat, harmonic tones of vintage fuzz faces, and cleans up like a classic Fender amp when you roll back your guitar's volume. Featuring hand-picked Germanium transistors, it delivers a vintage fuzz sound reminiscent of early Hendrix tones. The Contour knob allows you to dial in the midrange, harmonics, and sustain. Input Bias control removes the "woofiness" for overdrive/distortion sounds. Internal trimmer for clipping symmetry, harmonics, and tracking adjustment. Eric Johnson likes this one!
sources.snippet: Fulltone 69 Pedal mkII | AllThePedals
sources.bodyExcerpt: Fulltone 69 Pedal mkII | AllThePedals Articles Genealogy Browse Search results for " " Gain / Fuzz / Fulltone 69 Pedal mkII 69 Pedal mkII The Fulltone '69 mkII is a fuzz pedal designed to emulate the fat, harmonic tones of vintage fuzz faces, and cleans up like a classic Fender amp when you roll back your guitar's volume. Featuring hand-picked Germanium transistors, it delivers a vintage fuzz sound reminiscent of early Hendrix tones. The Contour knob allows you to dial in the midrange, harmonics, and sustain. Input Bias control removes the "woofiness" for overdrive/distortion sounds. Internal trimmer for clipping symmetry, harmonics, and tracking adjustment. Eric Johnson likes this one! What Fulltone say about the 69 Pedal mkII This is how you wished your Fuzzface sounded... Fat and Harmonic. And it cleans up like a vintage Fender amp when you turn down your guitar's volume control. The Rolling Stones and the Black Crowes have discovered this trick. If you love the first 2 Hendrix releases then you'll love this pedal, with 2 Germanium transistors hand-picked and tested for optimum performance. A Contour Knob lets you dial in Midrange, Harmonics and Sustain, also an Input Bias knob that takes out the "woofiness" and gives great Overdrive/Distortion sounds when its level is reduced. An Internal Trimmer allows for adjustment of Clipping Symmetry, Harmonics, and Tracking. Specifications subject to change at any given moment due to availability... and whimsy. True-Bypass w/LED is standard equipment to preserve tone when the pedal is off! Eric Johnson says of his '69... "Of all the pedals I've been sent... I like this one the best!" sources.title: Fulltone 70 Pedal-BC | AllThePedals
sources.description: The Fulltone '70 Pedal-BC delivers aggressive fuzz with a raw, vintage vibe. Featuring mismatched silicon transistors for a snarling, spitting tone, it's designed for players seeking authentic '70s fuzz sounds. With its mid control, the '70 Pedal-BC provides extra clarity and cut, and offers a unique character ideal for classic rock and blues. Compared to the ['69 Pedal](/pedals/fulltone-69-pedal-mkii), the '70 pedal goes further with its raw, untamed sound.
sources.snippet: Fulltone 70 Pedal-BC | AllThePedals
sources.bodyExcerpt: Fulltone 70 Pedal-BC | AllThePedals Articles Genealogy Browse Search results for " " Gain / Fuzz / Fulltone 70 Pedal-BC 70 Pedal-BC The Fulltone '70 Pedal-BC delivers aggressive fuzz with a raw, vintage vibe. Featuring mismatched silicon transistors for a snarling, spitting tone, it's designed for players seeking authentic '70s fuzz sounds. With its mid control, the '70 Pedal-BC provides extra clarity and cut, and offers a unique character ideal for classic rock and blues. Compared to the '69 Pedal , the '70 pedal goes further with its raw, untamed sound. What Fulltone say about the 70 Pedal-BC Ever played an original FuzzFace from around 1970? (HINT: Not AT ALL the same sound as ones with the same namesake being mass-produced currently.) Ours has two intentionally mismatched (for harmonic content) silicon transistors that snarl and spit... not for the meek! If you put the "Fuzz" on 10 you will rip, and you might get all sorts of oscillation and weirdness... but that's Rock. sources.description: Achieve natural, tubelike drive with the Full-Drive 2 V2. sources.title: Fulltone Full-Drive3 | AllThePedals
sources.description: The Fulltone Full-Drive 3 is an overdrive pedal known for its tube-like sound, achieved through JFET input and op-amp circuits. It offers versatile tonal options with a 3-way clipping switch, providing symmetrical clipping, wide asymmetrical settings, and a comp-cut mode for a volume boost. It also features independent overdrive and boost channels, and a buffered bypass. A Dynamics knob includes a Germanium diode Limiter circuit for enhanced feel and tonal control. The Full-Drive 3 aims to deliver the characteristics of various other gain effects, such as the [Marshall BluesBreaker](/pedals/marshall-bluesbreaker).
sources.snippet: Fulltone Full-Drive3 | AllThePedals
sources.bodyExcerpt: Fulltone Full-Drive3 | AllThePedals Articles Genealogy Browse Search results for " " Gain / Overdrive / Fulltone Full-Drive3 Full-Drive3 The Fulltone Full-Drive 3 is an overdrive pedal known for its tube-like sound, achieved through JFET input and op-amp circuits. It offers versatile tonal options with a 3-way clipping switch, providing symmetrical clipping, wide asymmetrical settings, and a comp-cut mode for a volume boost. It also features independent overdrive and boost channels, and a buffered bypass. A Dynamics knob includes a Germanium diode Limiter circuit for enhanced feel and tonal control. The Full-Drive 3 aims to deliver the characteristics of various other gain effects, such as the Marshall BluesBreaker . What Fulltone say about the Full-Drive3 Unlike its cousin the FD2, the FD3 uses both a JFET input and a JFET op-amp, giving it the most tube-like sound you can get out of a tubeless pedal. Along with great sound, these JFET’s give the FD3 an ultra-high Input impedance which allows the pedal to mate with any type/gain of pickup and react well to changes in your guitar’s volume control. 3-way CLIPPING toggle switch:set to 90’s and you’ll get symmetrical clipping with ample midrange.Set the switch to WIDE ASYM (wide asymmetrical) and more sweet highs and lows come through, along with chimey, Class-A style even harmonic overtones.set to COMP-CUT mode, pure opamp-overdrive, with no diode clipping assistance. Aggressive, cutting, and capable of a huge volume boost to slam the input of your amp. Discrete Channels:Unlike the FD2, the FD3 has completely independent OVERDRIVE and BOOST channels, and the ORDER toggle switch allows placing the BOOST channel* before* or after the OVERDRIVE channel. The BOOST channel is also an extremely transparent, high-headroom 100% JFET-powered circuit. Buffered Bypass:Serial# 2548 and higher FD3 pedals are now Buffered-Bypass instead of True-Bypass, so the FD3 will always drive long cables, be isolated from other effects, and always retain the highs and “feel” of your amplifier whether the pedal is turned ON or OFF. Do not confuse the hi-quality JFET op-amp buffer in the FD3 with the simple single transistor buffers on other pedals. The FD3's buffer sounds rich and fat, not thin. DYNAMICS knob:A Fulltone-exclusive Germanium diode Limiter circuit circuit that alters the feel of the notes being played as well as subdues transient spikes which can overload your amp’s input. This feature can make even a stiff amp feel responsive and juicy, and sweeten the treble frequencies. The Icing on the cake? The housing is about 20% smaller than the traditional FD2 SPECIFICATIONS:Input impedance: 1.1 mega-ohms. Output Impedance: 180 ohms. www.fulltoneusa.com Full-Drive3 compared to ... Equipped with a 3-way CLIPPING toggle switch, it allows you to switch between the smooth, symmetrical clipping of the familiar 1990s FD2, and the aggressive boost of pure op-amp overdrive with ample midrange, sweet highs and lows, and finely textured harmonics. The OVERDRIVE and BOOST channels are completely independent. The ORDER toggle switch allows you to place the BOOST channel either before or after the OVERDRIVE channel. The BOOST channel is an extremely transparent, high-headroom, 100% JFET-powered circuit with buffered bypass, maintaining the amp’s high-fidelity sound and feel whether it’s on or off. Turning up the DYNAMICS knob on the BOOST channel (Fulltone’s proprietary germanium diode limiter circuit) changes the feel of the sound, suppressing transient spikes that overload the amplifier input. This feature makes even a harsh amplifier feel responsive and juicy, and sweetens the high frequencies. It can be powered by 18V DC, allowing you to enjoy an even bigger sound with more headroom. Driven by a JFET input and JFET op-amp to deliver an exceptionally tubelike response, the Full-drive 3 serves up juicy crunch with all the trimmings. Flip the Full-drive 3’s Order switch to place the Boost either before or after the Overdrive section, but prepare to spend several hours exploring limitless tone-shaping options. Three different voicings let you choose between classic smooth, symmetrical clipping, contemporary Class A–style even harmonic overtones, and a searing Comp-cut setting that unleashes pure op-amp aggression — no diode clipping required.

sources.description: The Fulltone OCD-Germanium is a Custom Shop overdrive pedal featuring a unique circuit design with 2 Mosfets and 2 Germanium diodes. This pedal offers a tube-like feel, enhanced sustain, and a focused single-note tone. Experience a wider dynamic range and exceptional definition. Built in the USA, the OCD-Germanium delivers a versatile sound that sits between blues and greens. Explore the world of overdrive with this exceptional pedal.

This pedal offers a tube-like feel, enhanced sustain, and a focused single-note tone. Experience a wider dynamic range and exceptional definition. Built in the USA, the OCD-Germanium delivers a versatile sound that sits between blues and greens. Explore the world of overdrive with this exceptional pedal. What Fulltone say about the OCD-Germanium The OCD pedal is the only pedal that uses 2 x Mosfets configured as hard-clipping to 'Voltage reference" instead of the usual way: to ground." The earliest OCDs used 2 x Mosfets plus 1 x Germanium diode, but very quickly these diodes became harder and harder to find, and they became expensive. Recently I stumbled across a reasonably large stash of the right kind of Germanium diodes so I ponied-up and bought all of them. So I decided to do a run of the ultimate OCD: a Custom Shop offering with a few circuit tweaks using 2 x Mosfets plus 2 x Germanium diodes, and one hell of a beautiful paint job... Metallic Teal with a chrome undercoat! This beauty morphs between blues and greens depending on the light and angle. And what would the ultimate OCD be without a Blue LED? The sound? Great definition, more tube-like feel, a bit wider dynamic range, more sustain, and a more focused single-note tone. And as with all Fulltone pedals... 100% Built in the USA. www.fulltoneusa.com OCD-Germanium compared to ... NO RETURNS /LIMIT 2 PER HOUSEHOLD/ NO TAXES CHARGES / SHIPPING IS INCLUDED IN THE PRICE! About the OCD Born in 2004, The OCD has become one of the most sought after overdrives ever made, a fact born out by the many shitty Chinese-made clones being offered up by large companies too unscrupulous and cheap to license the real deal. They still haven’t got it right. V2 FEATURES: Output Buffer (when pedal is turned on I True-Bypass mode, or always when in Enhanced Bypass mode)) which eliminates it from being influenced be effects that came after it. Translation, your sound remains consistent regardless of placement in today’s more complex signal-chains, loopers, and pedalboards. This buffer also had a positive effect on the sound, it reduced loading on the pedal’s hard-clipping stage, allowing more sustain of both the sound and the overtones. Class A configured discrete 2N5457 JFET input section , raising the input impedance to 1 mega ohms (previously 330K) and increasing the dynamics…resulting in significantly better interaction with both single coil and humbuckers. Internal switch to choose between ”Enhanced Bypass TM ” True-Bypass, and with no popping sound in either mode. No other company offers EB…I invented it. A downside to True-Bypass: True-Bypass (TB) switching was the ultimate way to achieve a clean signal path for many years. Everything’s different now, most guitarists have elaborate pedalboards with 10 or more pedals being the norm, and tremendous potential for signal and tone loss with the many cables, connectors, and other pedals involved in the chain. There can be so much signal loss that it sounds nothing like the sound of a guitar with a cable straight into the front of a great tube amp. Uninspiring. What’s the pedal industries’ solution to this problem for the last 40 years? Unity-gain buffered bypass…i.e. a couple of Field effect Transistors (FETs) configured as unity-gain buffers ala Boss, Ibanez, etc, etc. What’s the benefit to unity-gain FET buffered bypass? It reduces the loading effect that occurs using long lengths of cable, and you remove the loud “popping” sound when switching the device on and off. What’s the issue with unity-gain FET buffered bypass? Although my ears always told me that it sounded “tinny” and that there was signal loss, with the help of a my favorite Electronic Engineer (using some very expensive test equipment) we recently documented that each unity-gain FET buffer actually cuts the gain somewhere between 0.3 to 0.6 dB. This loss of gain is in the low-Mids and Bass frequencies, resulting in that “tinny” sound now that the highs remained and some of the bass and mids are gone. Now factor in that there are two FETs per pedal required to couple the IN OUT path, that’s an obvious loss of between 1dB-2dB per pedal. What’s an even bigger issue with this old style unity-gain FET bypass? Show original For those who bought a Fulltone OCDv2 but don't know how to shape their sound | 3 settings to try first 1 ketunemikku 2026年9月20日 17:29 Hello, this is Ketsunemic. Once again, I would like to talk about the "Effector Explanation Sheet" project that I have been steadily working on recently. What I have completed this time is a two-page set for the Fulltone OCDv2. To begin with, why did I decide to summarize this on paper? The trigger was a very common scene. You get an effector, go home, and excitedly open the box. You plug it into an amp and step on the switch. …And then, what happens next? There are three knobs and one small switch. Even though it's just that, you suddenly don't know where or how to turn them. I remember this clearly myself. Starting with "everything at 12 o'clock for now," vaguely turning up the Drive, vaguely tweaking the Tone, and stopping at "well, I guess this is fine." And a few months later, that pedal quietly disappears from the board. This is by no means because the pedal was bad. It's just that no one told me where to place the first step . There is a mountain of information if you search online, but staring at your smartphone while playing is quite a mood killer. Something you can check just by dropping your gaze slightly while holding your guitar. I wish I had something like that at my feet. That thought was the starting point for this series. Page 1: "Sound Creation Guide" — A place to return to when you're lost "Sound Creation Guide." I have summarized the basic settings you want to learn first and the roles of the three knobs. So, here is the first page. There was only one thing I really wanted to convey on this page. VOLUME at 9 o'clock, DRIVE at 10 o'clock, TONE at 12 o'clock, and LP. This is the starting point for creating your sound with the OCDv2. It is not the correct answer. It is simply a starting point where "it's hard to get lost if you start here." On the top half of the page, I placed the roles of each of the three knobs along with an illustration of the unit itself. VOLUME is the output level. Let's try starting from a low position, I say. DRIVE is the amount of distortion. The more you turn it to the right, the more the distortion increases, I say. TONE is the brightness of the high-frequency range. Turning it to the right strengthens the highs, I say. And on the bottom right is the HP/LP toggle switch. I wrote, "Try LP first, and if you want to increase the distortion, compare it by listening to HP." For those who thought, "Isn't that obvious?" You are absolutely right. But I believe there is meaning in having this obvious information at hand in a form you can follow with your eyes while playing. On the bottom half, I prepared a section called "Do you have these concerns?" How far should I turn up the distortion? Are the highs too strong? Does the volume change when turned ON? These three are paths I have walked hundreds of times myself. For each, I briefly indicated only where to move: "Adjust VOLUME from a low position when the volume is different," "Move DRIVE little by little when comparing distortion," and "Move TONE little by little when the brightness bothers you." I haven't written the answers. Because the answers only exist in your room, with your amp, and in your ears. All I can do is point to where you should reach out. sources.title: Fulltone Octafuzz 2 | AllThePedals
sources.description: The Fulltone Octafuzz 2 is a precise recreation of the iconic Tycobrahe Octavia, delivering classic octave-up fuzz tones reminiscent of Hendrix's "Band of Gypsies" and SRV. Housed in a rugged steel enclosure, this pedal offers a unique, synth-like ring modulation and "steel-drum" vibe, making it ideal for creating distinctive fuzz sounds. It features a switch for a massive non-Octavia Fuzztone, a mod that other companies have adopted for their Tycobrahe reissues and clones. The Octafuzz 2 provides a range of unique fuzz tones, making it a great choice for guitarists looking for vintage fuzz.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Custom Shop Queen Bee (CS-QB) – Fulltone LLC | Online Store Fulltone Musical Products Log in or Create account Cart : 0 Search Menu Cart 0 Home Catalog + - Overdrive Distortion Fuzz Wah Wah Booster Modulation Delay Switching Cosmetic Blems Parts/Accessories Power Adapters One-Offs, Prototypes & Vintage Items Gift Cards News About Us E-News Signup Fulltone.com Log in Create account Search Fulltone Musical Products Home Catalog Overdrive Distortion Fuzz Wah Wah Booster Modulation Delay Switching Cosmetic Blems Parts/Accessories Power Adapters One-Offs, Prototypes Vintage Items Gift Cards News About Us E-News Signup Fulltone.com Home › Custom Shop Queen Bee (CS-QB) Custom Shop Queen Bee (CS-QB) $ 0.00 Default Title - See Below for Availability Quantity Add to Cart These are 100% handmade with full-size components here is Nashville. The Custom Shop Queen Bee is powered by 3 x New Old Stock Military “Flying Saucer” germanium transistors in an original design that behaves in an amp-like manner, meaning it responds dynamically to the input from your hands and guitar. Great clean-up by lowering the guitar’s volume knob, sweet mids, clarity, sustain, harmonics...it’s all in there. The #1 and #2 transistors are configured to achieve maximum gain in order to hit transistor #3 extremely hard, creating more sustain and distortion than is possible with the 2-transistor Fuzzes while making the pedal rather low-noise for such a high-gained design. Another thing the Bee has, something no other fuzzes have, is ample MIDRANGE! Fender amp owners will appreciate the Passive Hi-Cut Tone control for taming the treble, and further sonic sculpting is accomplished via a smart, loss-less 3-position Bass switch (placed before transistor #3) tailoring the low frequencies and keeping the bottom-end tight. Looking at this pedal’s signal on an oscilloscope reveals what your ears already knew...a wildly asymmetrical waveform high in second-order Harmonics, culminating in a sweet, rich, commanding voice with tons of sustain. Translation: This pedal will not get lost in the mix. Inside the pedal is a trimmer for adjusting the bias of transistor #3 by a range between 2 and 6 volts DC. My favorite tending to be somewhere between 3 and 4 volts. The trimmer should be adjusted by ear as there are no wrong settings, a slight turn results in a drastic change in sound, in volume, and in compression characteristics. Suddenly firm becomes soft, bright becomes warm, grainy becomes smooth...it’s astonishing what this little trimmer does. As with most Fulltone pedals, the Queen Bee has True-Bypass switching via the Fulltone 3PDT footswitch for maximum signal integrity while the pedal is bypassed. Because the Bee utilizes Germanium transistors it should only be powered with the (included) battery or a dedicated (not shared!) “Center Positive,” well-regulated power supply. Do not “daisy-chain” multiple pedals on a single wall wart adapter as this may damage the pedal. Instead the Queen Bee should be connected to its own outlet on a professional-grade power supply that has regulated, isolated/discrete outputs, in addition a reversed power cable must be used. Fulltone Queen Bees are 100% Hand-Built in the USA. Equipped with 3 gain-matched germanium transistor for a FAT, searing lead tone, Fulltone also made the Tone control response and range more usable and much less shrill sounding... Full clockwise is SMOOTH sounding. The Soul-Bender cleans up when you back-off on the guitar's volume control. This pedal has tons of tonal character and even harmonics and of course, true bypass w/ LED is included with every one. V2 is a huge improvement in the way the 3rd transistor is biased, making every single one consistently epic sounding! sources.bodyExcerpt: Guitar Pedal X - GPX Blog - Fulltone USA reissues and reboots its celebrated Ultimate Octave Upper Octave Fuzz - now in improved Compact Edition ao link News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Xploration • Curation • Recommendation News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Filter content by area of interest Amps Boost and Overdrive Delay Distortion Fuzz Guitars Modulation Pitch Reverb Utility All All Fulltone USA reissues and reboots its celebrated Ultimate Octave Upper Octave Fuzz - now in improved Compact Edition Nov 13, 2025 15:00 by Stefan Karlsson Fulltone Effects Fuzz Octave Fuzz Full Article Read Summary Key Points Fulltone USA is reissuing the Ultimate Octave Upper Octave Fuzz in a smaller Compact Edition with full-size THT Components and top-mounted jacks. It has Volume, Fuzz, Tone, and Bright/Fat EQ Voice controls, plus independent Fuzz and Octave-On/Off footswitches. Fat mode gives warm, classic vocal-like fuzz with punchy mids; Bright mode adds a mid scoop with Bass and Treble boost. Features include True Bypass, hand-made-in-the-USA construction, and optional 9–18V DC power. The stated price was $290 / £289. International Dealers should receive it imminently. No new demos were available; older-model demos were used initially. Back by popular demand as the saying goes. We now get an evolved format of the Fulltone Ultimate Octave - in a much shrunk down and modernised pedalboard-friendly - still with full-size high quality THT Components - but with top-mounted jacks too. The Ultimate Octave has the perfect complement of controls with the Octave On/Off on the second footswitch, and an additional really handy Bright / Fat EQ Switch. Controls - Volume, Fuzz, Tone, EQ Voice : Bright / Fat, On/Off Footswitch, Octave-Up Footswitch. The Ultimate Octave Fuzz goes for $290 / £289 and equivalent from the Fulltone USA Webstore . And it should be available imminently at International Dealers. I will almost certainly be getting one for myself - but not sure if it will happen this year or next! It definitely goes onto the list! Key Features The return of Fulltone’s legendary Octave Fuzz pedal Independent footswitches for Fuzz and Octave The Fat/Bright voice toggle completely reshapes the EQ curve and gain structure: Fat mode : Warm, classic vocal-like fuzz with punchy mids Bright mode : Mid scoop with Bass and Treble boost Top-mounted jacks Compact custom enclosure True Bypass switching Hand-made in the USA Powered by (opt.) 9-18V DC PSU (centre -, 2.1mm, ~ 35 mA current draw, not included) There don’t seem to be any new demos yet - I’ve waited a while for one to materialise - but it doesn’t seem to be coming in any hurry - so I will initially make use of one of the older format demos! And will update of course whenever the new demos materialise! sources.description: The Fuzzrocious Cat Tail is a versatile distortion pedal with overdrive and fuzz-like characteristics at higher gain settings. Based on a classic distortion circuit, it's been modified for guitar and bass use. Features include a diode toggle for clipping options and the Beavis double resistor mod for fine-tuning your sound.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Fuzzrocious Pedals CAT TAIL | AllThePedals Articles Genealogy Browse Search results for " " Gain / Distortion / Fuzzrocious Pedals CAT TAIL CAT TAIL The Fuzzrocious Cat Tail is a versatile distortion pedal with overdrive and fuzz-like characteristics at higher gain settings. Based on a classic distortion circuit, it's been modified for guitar and bass use. Features include a diode toggle for clipping options and the Beavis double resistor mod for fine-tuning your sound. What Fuzzrocious Pedals say about the CAT TAIL What is the CAT TAIL? The Cat Tail is a low to high gain distortion with overdrive capabilities (some even say at high gain settings, it sounds like a fuzz). This circuit is based on a well-loved, classic distortion that make a clean amp dirty and a dirty amp disgusting. We have tweaked the original circuit to better meet the needs of guitarists and bassists alike. With the addition of a diode toggle for extra tweakability for clipping options, we have added to the modifications the Beavis double resistor mod (Clipping 1 and 2 pots) to allow the user to subtly fine tune how the signal clips on the highs and lows. Please view the for more information about this pedal. PLEASE NOTE: This is in fact the pedal known formerly known as “Rat Tail.” We changed the name in July 2015 to avoid product confusion. The circuit remains the same. fuzzrociouspedals.com CAT TAIL compared to ... sources.bodyExcerpt: FUZZROCIOUS PEDALS CAT TAIL MANUAL Pdf Download | ManualsLib Sign In Upload Download Table of Contents Contents Add to my manuals Delete from my manuals Share URL of this page: HTML Link: FUZZROCIOUS PEDALS CAT TAIL MANUAL Pdf Download '> Pinterest Bookmark this page Add Manual will be automatically added to "My Manuals" Print this page × Bookmark added × Added to my manuals Manuals Brands Fuzzrocious pedals Manuals Music Pedal CAT TAIL Manual Fuzzrocious pedals CAT TAIL Manual Hide thumbs 1 2 page of 2 Go / 2 Contents Table of Contents Bookmarks Table of Contents 1 About 2 Controls 3 Mods 4 Power 5 Paint 6 Layout Examples Download this manual ABOUT The Cat Tail is a low to high gain distortion with overdrive capabilities (some even say at high gain settings, it sounds like a fuzz). This circuit is based on a well-loved, classic distortion that make a clean amp dirty and a dirty amp disgusting. We have tweaked the original circuit to better meet the needs of guitarists and bassists alike. With the addition of a diode toggle for extra tweakability for clipping options, we have added to the modifications the Beavis double resistor mod (Clipping 1 and 2 pots) to allow the user to subtly fine tune how the signal clips on the highs and lows. Please note – The Cat Tail is the same pedal/circuit as the pedal formerly known as CONTROLS VOLUME – makes the output of the circuit louder or quieter. TONE FILTER – moves from treble to bass when turned clockwise. There is a general high mids presence in most tone settings with little to no bass loss. DISTORTION – moves from a little to no drive/distortion to high distortion when turned clockwise. CLIPPING 1 2 POTS – fine tunes how the signal clips on the highs and lows. To start, roll them both back, then slowly roll them clockwise to find your personal taste in clipping of your signal. DIODE TOGGLE– changes the clipping diodes from 1n914 silicon to no diodes to LEDs. MODS FEEDBACK MOD - via a momentary or latching footswitch connected to a feedback pot, one can feed the signal back upon itself for oscillation/feedback/nois. Tail will negate the feedback mod. KILLSWITCH MOD - via a momentary footswitch, one can mute the sound passing through the pedal. Hit it rhythmically to a tempo or sporadically. Get weird with it. 2 DISTORTION MOD - via a latching footswitch, one can switch back and forth between two (2) distortion pots. Think of it like having nd two distortion presets and using a footswitch to move back and forth between the two. Distortion is not stacking. POWER Fuzzrocious Pedals' products do not support batteries due to risk of damage to the unit and for ecological concerns related to the use and disposal of batteries. It is the customer's responsibility to power the pedal with a 9V DC 2.1mm center negative tip adaptor that will not be provided by Fuzzrocious Pedals, LLC. PAINT All handpainted pedals, unless otherwise specified are painted with enamel or acrylic paint by Shannon Ratajski. Some pedals are painted by the Ratajski children. Powdercoating and screenprinting for pedals sold through dealers are done locally by Juxtaprints. http://fuzzrociouspedals.com ||| fuzzrociouspedals@gmail.com For information about warranties, please visit http://fuzzrociouspedals.com/termsandconditions. sources.description: Overdrive and Distortion The past is only a sonic guide with this versatile and highly-capable drive/distortion. As your guitar signal enters the Outlier it receives a hero’s welcome with nearly every amenity imaginable. Consider the internal signal chain: Op-Amp Buffered Input gt; Op-Amp Gain Stage gt; FET Gain Stage gt; Op-Amp Gain Stage gt; Cabinet Simulator gt; Active EQ gt; Volume Control gt; BJT Output Buffer. What does this even mean?! The Outlier represents the miniaturization of a whole series of circuitry functions and combines them into one unit while disguising their capability in an easy to use drive pedal with typical controls that can access all the power and control that the complex structure offers. 3 cascading gain-stages seamlessly glide from low gain settings that sound full and robust to high gain settings that lack nothing for dynamic and definable complete saturation. Active EQ makes the difference in allowing the user to take true control of tonal shaping rather than the reductive process of passive EQ. No expense has been spared to get every little edge one could want out of a compact drive circuit. We’ll say no more and let your experience with the Outlier be the judge.

Greenhouse Effects Greenhouse Effects 27 Club series browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Greenhouse Effects Remedy Published on April 2, 2010 Greenhouse Effects 27 Club series fuzz pedal Information Greenhouse Effects When it comes to fuzz, it's all about character - And this fuzz has a unique and distinctive one. A blend of silicon and germanium transistors pushed to near melting point, creates a variety of intense and powerful fuzz tones, from 60's psychedelic garage fuzz to extreme uncompromising stoner growl. The health knob has a dramatic effect on the way this pedal acts and sounds. Fully clockwise, the fuzz is at its best shape - aggressive , jumpy and loud. Turn the health down and make it sweat - this fuzz sounds crazier as it struggle to fight back. Finally it submits and delivers a sweet gargle, making your guitar sound like a disrupted brass instrument. Use the health knob when the fuzz knob is near maximum or tweak the fuzz and health knobs for different sounds. You can always tone things down by using your guitar volume knob. you'll be rewarded with a sweet velvety decay. True bypass! Greer Amps browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Greer Amps 390 Vintage OD Preamp Published on March 9, 2014 Greer Amps distortion pedal Controls Level Gain Information Greer Amplification The Greer Amps Custom Shop 390 Vintage OD/Preamp came about after a request from one of our first endorsers. Seeking a vintage sounding overdrive that can get harmonic crunch, Mr. Casey Meyer asked us to build him a pedal that was modeled after the vintage DOD Overdrive Preamp 250. This is our answer. The 390 is an awesome sounding drive, featuring only two controls--Gain and Volume. This pedal can go from light grit to nasty snarl with the turn of the Gain control. Featuring a vintage-correct LM741 chip, this pedal sounds awesome. Now...did we just go and copy the old pedal? Hah. Nope. We changed some things around. We upgraded all components, including all signal capacitors (Panasonic ECQ series and Nichicon KW audio series capacitors), resistors (metal film where needed for noise reduction), and even added diode protection and some light power filtering to help out when the 390 is running on a power supply. This pedal is currently limited to the first run of 30 total pieces. Don't wait...order NOW! This pedal features a high contrast, laser etched, black and white faceplate, with white knobs, so you can see your settings on a dark stage. The 390 also features true bypass, like all Greer Amps pedals, and runs off a standard 9 volt, 2.1mm, negative center power supply. We recommend using a high quality, regulated, and filtered power supply with all of our pedals. Vintage overdrive tones to harmonic crunch! Bold tones, asymmetrical clipping! Based on the DOD 250, with upgrades! High contrast black/white faceplate, with white knobs, to easily view settings on a dark stage! Hand wired in Athens, GA! True Bypass! Uses 9Volt battery or standard neg. center, 2.1mm power supply. Built with top quality components. Lifetime Warranty to the original owner! Pedals are currently built to order, and ship within 1-2 weeks of the order being placed, and funds entering our account! Limited first run - 30 pieces available. Посмотрите похожие товары Быстрый просмотр Nux NOD-2 Tube Man MKII гитарный эффект overdrive 3490 ₽ Быстрый просмотр Electro-Harmonix Nano Operation Overlord гитарный эффект overdrive / distortion 8990 ₽ Быстрый просмотр Boss SD-1 Super OverDrive гитарный эффект overdrive 9190 ₽ Быстрый просмотр DV Mark Over Marker гитарный эффект overdrive 9990 ₽ Быстрый просмотр Joyo JF-02 Ultimate Drive гитарный эффект overdrive 3150 ₽ Быстрый просмотр MXR M77 Custom Badass Modified O.D. гитарный эффект overdrive 16690 ₽ Быстрый просмотр Joyo R-21 Tornado гитарный эффект overdrive 9190 ₽ Быстрый просмотр Strymon Riverside гитарный эффект overdrive / distortion 36990 ₽ Основные характеристики Производитель Greer Amps Страна производства США Срок гарантии 12 месяцев Greer Amps 390 Vintage OD/Preamp – гитарная педаль-овердрайв/преамп, построенная на винтажно-корректном чипе LM471. Скажу сразу по-честному: 390 Vintage OD/Preamp построен на схеме известного овердрайва DOD 250 Overdrive/Preamp. Как и DOD, 390 способен выдавать разные типы звучания от клин-буста до самостоятельного овердрайва с лёгким оттенком фузза. Особенно удобно педаль чувствует себя перед “разогретым” усилителем, увеличивая уровень гейна и раскрывая характер самого усилителя – в конце концов, в 70-е годы педали и делали для того, чтобы заставлять усилители жужжать сильнее! Особенности частотной характеристики оригинальной педали DOD 250 – а именно её “честность” и “прозрачность” – аккуратно и прилежно сохранены. Кстати, благодаря этой “честности” эта схема отлично обходится без потенциометра тона – здесь действует простая философия: “получил – перегрузил – отдаю”, без особенно резких бустов или срезов АЧХ. Что мы всё рассуждаем в стиле “как у DOD 250”? Greer Amps – не те ребята, которые станут просто собирать известную схему и продавать её в красивой коробке (вы только взгляните на их бороды!). Поэтому 390 – это существенно модифицированный или улучшенный 250 (аж на 140!). Произведена ревизия используемых компонентов, благодаря которой звучание педали стало ещё более сочным, а количество шумов – просто ничтожным как в случае питания батарейкой, так и в случае использования блока питания. К слову, в прошлом году, через 40 лет после своего первого издания, в строй вернулся оригинальный DOD 250. Сможет ли Земля выдержать битву этих титанов? Управление: Level – уровень громкости. Положение “Ъ” находится около трёх часов, потому как педаль просится согреть Ваш замерзающий усилитель. Gain – уровень перегруза – меньше, чем нынче можно, но больше, чем можно ожидать от реплики винтаж

sources.bodyExcerpt: Greer Amps Black Mountain Crunch Drive - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Greer Amps Black Mountain Crunch Drive Posted By Pedal of the Day on Saturday, April 26, 2025 in Greer Amps, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments --> --> Today’s pedal is kind of a special one – last fall, I donated money to a raffle that Waterslide Guitars was having to benefit the World Central Kitchen , who have helped feed people in and around Asheville, NC, where I happen to live, in the wake of Hurricane Helene. To my surprise, my name was chose as the winner of the Greer Amps Black Mountain Crunch Drive, and I couldn’t have been happier. It’s been a while since a Greer pedal came through the shop, and I was stoked to check this one out, as always… Shop Greer Amps at Amazon https://amzn.to/4jl9wdh Looming large, like the towering behemoths of full stacks of yore, the Black Mountain Crunch Drive roars to life, bringing new dimensions of vintage tone to guitarists (and bass players, too!). This new crunch based drive is rooted in a tone quest for the sound of one particular recording of a crunchy British amp , but it has flexibility beyond just that sound. From simply adding crunch, to getting that famous midrange snarl and growl of those metal panel amps that came out just after the plexi era, the Black Mountain Crunch Drive gives up the goods in a way that has a natural, amp-like crunch to it. This circuit was inspired by many conversations with many friends, and developed with The Darkness’ album Permission to Land blasting in the background…it’ll get ya there, if you want it to. The two clipping diodes responsible for the drive in this circuit are purposefully imbalanced, selected to impart the proper texture and crunch for this circuit. This pedal gives you giant, stack-based crunch overdrive , as well as midrange snarl and texture like giant old stacks of yore! The raffle that the Black Mountain Crunch Drive came from was a big success, raising almost $11,000 for the World Central Kitchen. I can’t say enough about all the donations, hard work and effort that people from this area and people from all over contributed during such a tough time. It’s gonna be a while before Asheville and the surrounding areas are back to full strength, if ever, but WNC is strong, and we’ll keep rebuilding, especially with folks like Waterslide Guitars and Greer Amps helping along the way. Be sure to visit both of their websites and grab some gear, and don’t forget to check out our demo video below – cheers! Based on the brownface Fender Concert, Greer Amps has put the legendary sound and feel of this amp literally at your feet. A FET based circuit, capable of producing a full spectrum of clean to amp-like overdrive, the Brown Bomber sounds and reacts like an amp in every way. How is this possible? The circuitry of the pedal is very similar to the actual circuit of the Concert, but with FETs in place of tubes. Atop the pedal sits controls for Volume, Bass, Treble, Gain, and Presence. The pedal captures the Fendery top end, and growly midrange of these brownface classics. FETs in pedal are indvidually preset for their optimum bias range, and not for user tweaking. sources.description: The Green Giant is not your typical distortion pedal. This is a hard to find pedal, but also fun and easy to build. Check it out.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Greer Amps Green Giant On Stripboard - Crazy Chicken Guitar Pedals Skip to content Home Beginners Guide Stripboard Layouts Easy Builds Component Guides Handy Reference Articles About Privacy Policy Returns Policy Blog Shop Contact Cart Home Beginners Guide Stripboard Layouts Easy Builds Component Guides Handy Reference Articles About Privacy Policy Returns Policy Blog Shop Contact Cart Greer Amps Green Giant On Stripboard August 28, 2024 Categories: Guitar Pedal Builds Here’s a kind of weird guitar pedal, but a fun build nonetheless and also a pretty simple guitar pedal build too. I had never heard of the Green Giant by Greer Amps before and I kind of just stumbled upon the layout on Tagboard Effects and thought it sounded interesting. Other than what’s on Tagboard Effects, I can’t find any more information on this pedal. Everyone else on the internet appears to have the same brief description of the pedal that you see at Tagboard Effects. The Greer website doesn’t even have any information on the pedal. What I do know from the brief description that’s repeated across the internet is that the Green Giant was never a production pedal. Instead it was only built for “endorsers.” I assume that these were artists who had some sort of endorsement relationship with Greet Amps. The Green Giant is a modification of Greer Amps’ existing Black Fuzz pedal, which in itself is just a modified Electra Distortion circuit , which is a very popular starting point for a lot of fuzz, distortion, and overdrive circuits, the Lovepedal Champ being one of them. The big difference with the Green Giant when compared to Greer Amps’ Black Fuzz is the introduction of the blend dial. This affects how much the signal is getting clipped by the clipping diodes and how much clean signal is getting through. Rather than just giving levels of distortion from “not so distorted” up to “very distorted,” the blend knob on the Green Giant allows some clean signal through while also allowing some distorted signal through. So it’s not just levels, it’s a mixture of clean and dirty signals. I did manage to use the Wayback Machine to find a product listing from 2016 for this pedal on the Greer website, but it didn’t offer much more information than what I had already seen.For whatever reason Greer decided to discontinue this pedal and it hasn’t been talked about very much. Jump to stripboard layout . Greer Amps Green Giant Wiring Schematic I’ll jump into the stripboard layout later in the article, but below is the wiring schematic for the Green Giant. As mentioned in the intro to this article, there’s not a lot of information on this pedal out there, and I could only find one source on the schematic. I compared this to the stripboard layout and there were a couple minor differences, but I think I’ve managed to piece everything together into something that at least resembles the original schematic. Unfortunately this isn’t readily verifiable information. With a lot of these pedals I can often find original information on the schematic or at least enough sources to verify it. In this case, I couldn’t, but I do know the schematic (and the stripboard layout below) works! So if you like this pedal build, it may not be the exact way it was done by Greer Amps, but it’s also probably close enough. Here’s the wiring diagram: Click on the schematic to enlarge it. And here’s the bill of materials. Notes R1 1M R2 2.2M R3 47K R4 680R C1 100nF C2 100nF Q1 2N3904 P1 25K Lin Clean mix potentiometer P2 100K Log Volume potentiometer D1, D2 1N4148 Jacks, power supply, etc. Don't Forget The stuff you usually use. Yep, it’s clearly an Electra Distortion, but that’s OK, it’s the circuit that just keeps on giving! The obvious addition here is the potentiometer wired in just before the clipping diodes. Clean Mix sweeps dirt to full fuzz. The Green Giant was never a production pedal. It was only built for endorsers who had a relationship with Greer Amps, making it a rare piece for collectors. The circuit is a modification of the Black Fuzz, itself a modified Electra Distortion circuit. The big difference is the addition of a Blend dial (labeled Clean Mix). This affects how much signal gets clipped by the diodes versus how much clean signal passes through. Oddly, the amount of distortion increases as you turn the Clean Mix knob to the left, which is by design. Two knobs total: Volume and Clean Mix. You can sweeten your tone by mixing in just the right amount of dirt, or run it as a full-on Black Fuzz with the blend dialed all the way down. R ock G uitars S tories P eople F orever Search GuitarGangsters ⌕ Menu Home Guitar Legends Gear Rigs Guitars Amps Pedals & FX Pickups Accessories DIY Builds Custom Builds Electronics & Wiring Finishing & Relics Mods & Upgrades Rock History 70’s Rock 80’s Metal 90’s Grunge & Alternative 2000’s Revival News Culture Videos About Contact In this guide The short version Athens, Georgia, and a grandfather’s advice The epoxy Specifications The Freq knob, and why one EQ control beats two Famous players — and what is actually documented Tone recipes How it compares Buying guide, September 2026 The honest negatives Who should not buy this pedal Living with one Frequently asked questions In this guide The short version Athens, Georgia, and a grandfather’s advice The epoxy Specifications The Freq knob, and why one EQ control beats two Famous players — and what is actually documented Tone recipes How it compares Buying guide, September 2026 The honest negatives Who should not buy this pedal Living with one Frequently asked questions Share this article Home › Gear Rigs › Greer Lightspeed Organic Overdrive: The Pedal That Wins By Not Being Noticed Gear Rigs Greer Lightspeed Organic Overdrive: The Pedal That Wins By Not Being Noticed Greer Lightspeed Organic Overdrive guide: the epoxy-potted circuit, the Freq knob explained, verified players, tone recipes and 2026 buying advice. admin 22 September 2026 20 min read GG-ARTICLE-TOP Every boutique overdrive on earth claims to be transparent. Almost none of them are, and the ones that come closest tend to be the ones that talk about it least. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO The Greer Lightspeed talks about it least. It has no toggles, no internal trimmers, no clipping-diode menu, no boutique origin myth involving a rediscovered NOS transistor. It has three knobs, a bare aluminium box with an engraved faceplate, and a circuit board deliberately buried in epoxy so nobody can copy it. That is the entire proposition. And somehow this is the pedal that ends up permanently switched on under the feet of Jason Isbell, Tom Bukovac, Daniel Donato, Dweezil Zappa and half of Nashville’s session floor. Ask an owner what it does and you will usually get some version of the same answer: nothing you can point at, and everything you’d miss. That is a strange thing to spend $249 on. It is also, twelve years after Premier Guitar handed it a Gear Award, why the Lightspeed has not been discontinued, redesigned or superseded — because there is nothing in it to fix. How to Get the Tone ↓ The short version The Greer Amps Lightspeed Organic Overdrive is a low-to-medium-gain overdrive built by hand in Athens, Georgia. Three controls: Loudness (output), Drive (gain) and Freq (a single sweeping EQ control that adds bass presence below noon and upper mids above it). True bypass. 9V battery or 9–18V DC external supply. 11 mA current draw at 9 volts. Its gain range starts at genuinely clean and tops out somewhere in mild crunch. It will not do distortion, it will not do metal, and it is a poor choice for stacking into an already-saturated high-gain rig. What it does instead is thicken, sustain and slightly sweeten whatever is already there — which is why the phrase that keeps recurring in owner discussions is not “boost” or “drive” but “channel 2” : a second voice for a single-channel amp that costs nothing in character. Price as of September 2026: $249 direct from Greer , typically $229 at US dealers , with used units on Reverb starting around $210 . That is expensive for three knobs, and it was the only complaint Premier Guitar could find in 2014. It is still the only real complaint now. Plexi spirit in pedal form, tight lows, smooth highs. The Little Samson was built at the request of Andy Elliott of Elliott Guitars, who wanted a do-it-all drive with natural, higher gain that still stays full. It's the highest-gain cousin to the Lightspeed and Southland, delivering chunky drive with crunched-out distortion and singing lead tones. Despite the high gain capability, it never gets buzzy or flubby. The high end stays smooth with proper treble, lows remain tight and amazingly balanced, and the midrange sits right where it needs to be. Volume, Gain, and Tone provide a huge range of drive and distortion territory. The pedal captures the spirit of old Marshall Plexi amps in a clean, crisp package. Mizuki (noun, Japanese origin) —A term meaning “beautiful moon.” Mizuki Blue is a dual-JFET overdrive pedal designed to replicate the feel and dynamics of two cascading tube gain stages. JFET transistors were created to emulate the warm, responsive character of tubes in a solid-state format, and Mizuki Blue puts them to work—one stage driving the other into rich, chewy overdrive. From fat vintage grunt to a clear, musical boost, this circuit covers a wide tonal spectrum. The simple three-knob layout makes it easy to dial in tones for everything from jazz and country to classic and hard rock. It stacks beautifully with other drives, adding depth, complexity, and harmonic richness to your sound. Mizuki Blue isn’t just another gain stage—it’s a tone-shaping weapon. Kick it in front of your favorite drive for searing saturation, drop it behind for a powerful boost, or let it stand alone into your amp for raw grit and rich texture. We’ve even pushed it straight into recording interfaces to capture wild, blown-out character and fuzz-like tones that cut through any mix. Mizuki Blue runs off of a standard 9 volt power supply with a negative center pin, and can be ran up to 18 volts for more headroom and output volume. ***Mizuki Blue has trim pots inside, they set the bias of the JFETs they should NOT be adjusted, as doing so will cause the pedal to cease working or function improperly. The Greer Amps Moonshot is our take on a true classic circuit. This pedal is inspired by vintage Germanium preamp circuits of days gone past. Featuring two controls, the Moonshot has a great tonal range, and can provide wonderful texture, when pushing the front end of an amplifier. The Treble/Mid control allows the player to set this pedal as a treble booster, or roll some extra low-end into the circuit, giving more midrange girth and grunt from the Germanium AC-128 transistor. The Master Volume control allows the user to push an amp into snarly overdrive. The Moonshot’s circuit features a voltage inverter, to run the transistor in proper, positive ground mode, while using a standard negative ground power supply. The Mori Drive: for years, we have been asked to build a drive based on that old vintage standby that so many love with the famous “mid hump”…we have finally landed on a set of tweaks with this type of circuit that we believe fits with the other drives in our line, and makes all of our test amps sing. Available to Greer Amps artists only for a while, what is now known as Mori Drive is inspired by vintage TS circuitry, tuned between TS and K-style frequency ranges…it’s my personal favorite set of mods for that circuit and uses a JRC4558 chip. I’ve built a ton of TS type circuits for folks over the years and this one is the one that I think is the “Greer signature” type sound and feel for that circuit. The mid hump on the Mori Drive is positioned in a sonically pleasing area, and there is more output volume available when compared to a standard TS type circuit. Clipping is also tweaked, to achieve a smoother tone that blends so very well with a pushed amp, and stacks amazingly with your other drives. We have stacked this pedal with every single drive circuit that we have built, and with many other companies’ drives, and we have yet to find a bad combination. What happens when you run one old school transistor based gain stage into another one, and use them as a drive-meets-distortion!? Well...you get the Peacemaker. We've built this pedal for about 20 years or so now, doing small batch runs here and there. These are fun pedals that can do a slight "vintage feeling and sounding" eq shift with boost capabilities, or they can push into drive meets distortion territory. The sound is very much a transistor drive-distortion sound, and has a very unique and fun character to it. Slam a tube amp with this pedal, and it's a dream. This pedal requires a 9 volt battery or 9 volt DC power supply, in the standard negative center pin configuration. It's simple, it sounds great, and it's a lot of fun. There's no way to fluff this up, so I won't try to do so. If you want something that will make you smile with a Strat, Tele, or a Les Paul...you found it...personally, I like having fun...do you? sources.bodyExcerpt: Greer Amps Peacemaker Distortion - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Greer Amps Peacemaker Distortion Posted By Pedal of the Day on Saturday, September 26, 2015 in Greer Amps, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments --> --> As you may or may not have figured out by now, we here at Pedal of the Day are BIG fans of Nick and Greer Amps, and love it when a new pedal of theirs shows up on the doorstep. Today’s pedal seems to have flown a bit under the radar, as you can’t even purchase it on their website (I had to search to find this one used), which makes it all the more interesting: today’s gem of a pedal is the Peacemaker Dual Class A Transistor Distortion. While this pedal’s official title is a “distortion”, it feels and sounds much more like an overdrive/boost to me, although it can get pretty crunchy when cranked. With only two controls knobs, it’s a really simple piece of gear to use, and great sounds can be dialed in within minutes of first turning it on. The Power and Preamp knobs represent two unique gain stages, and work well solo or running together. This pedal is capable of doing a great clean boost if you want it to, but the real power and fun of it lies when both knobs are cranked to at least noon, and the further right you keep turning them, the more growl, grit and distortion you’ll be able to conjure up, until your amp is singing with overdrive and sparkling with tone. In doing my research for this pedal, I discovered that there seems to be an earlier version of this, a big, hand-painted(?) box with chicken knobs and hand-written text. I personally like the deep gray color and compact size of this new version, and regardless of what it looks like, it sounds like a million bucks. If you need a little added sparkle and pizazz for you rig, you really should give the Peacemaker from Greer Amps a go. sources.bodyExcerpt: Greer Amps Relic Drive - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Greer Amps Relic Drive Posted By Pedal of the Day on Thursday, January 14, 2016 in Greer Amps, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments --> --> There are a lot of “Screamer” pedals out in the world, being manufactured by a ton of different companies, and rightly so, as it was one of the first truly awesome overdrive pedals in existence. However, with so many floating around, it’s sometimes hard to decipher which one is from where, as they can tend to all start to sound fairly similar. Enter today’s pedal, the Relic Drive from our friends at Greer Amp in Athens, GA. Certainly a take on the big green monster, this pedal has a few differences, as well as a couple of tricks up its sleeves. The controls are basically what you’d expect to find: Volume puts out the overall loudness of the Relic Drive, Gain adjusts how heavy the pedal’s sound is, and Tone moves the frequency from low to high and everywhere in between, with a wide frequency response to go from Dark and brooding to bright and sharp in a second. In contrast to most of these type of overdrives, however, Nick and crew have moved the mid hump to a warmer, more guitar friendly area, making the overall tone a bit fatter. Plus, there’s more Gain than usual on tap with the Relic Drive, making it perfect for both a boost/light drive function, as well as a bigger, louder but harmonic overdrive sound. These improvements and additions really bring out the power and pizazz of the Relic Drive, and truly launch it into a new category of screaming overdrive. As with all Greer Amps pedals, this beauty is true bypass, and built with lots of high-quality components and love in Athens, GA. If by some slim chance you’ve never had the pleasure of playing any of Nick’s pedals, do yourself a favor – go to their website and pick anything to try, I promise you won’t be disappointed that you did! Home About Us PRODUCTS ▾ Pedals Amps Merch Merch Dealers-Artists ▾ Dealers Artists Contact Us ▾ CONTACT WARRANTY REPAIRS POLICIES Cart Home / Products / SOMA 63 Vintage Preamp SOMA 63 Vintage Preamp $229.00 Qty Add to Cart Enclosure Dimensions (in): 4.77" x 2.6" x 1.39" Power: 9-18 volt neg. center pin ONLY. Current draw: 10mA @ 9v, 18mA @ 18V. A brave new world of tone, the SOMA ‘63 Vintage Preamp is the first pedal in the XFR series of pedals from Greer Amps. The SOMA ’63 is a true vintage preamp, based on the tone and feel of vintage brown era amplifiers from California. This pedal simulates the entire preamp, phase inverter, power section, and even the feel of the vintage 10 inch Utah speakers that were in those famous brown amps. The tone stack is designed to provide a wide and dynamic range of tonal options to the user. The Presence control works with the tone stack, and is designed to be a wide range control, effecting the overall sound of the entire circuit. The SOMA ’63 features a steel core transformer in the audio signal path. The transformer lends to the overall tone shaping of the circuit, and when the gain is pushed hard, especially with higher output pickups, the small steel core transformer will saturate, just like a vintage amplifier. The SOMA ’63 can be used as a tone-shaping preamp, or as an overdrive pedal. There are a wide variety of tones available in the SOMA ’63, so spend some time with your new pedal, and find the tones that rock your world! The SOMA ‘63 runs off of a standard, negative center pin 9 volt power supply, and can be ran off of up to 18 volts. At 9 volts, the SOMA ‘63 will have more grit and texture. The SOMA 63 is a true vintage preamp, based on the tone and feel of vintage brown era amplifiers from California. This pedal simulates the entire preamp, phase inverter, power section, and even the feel of the vintage 10 inch Utah speakers that were in those famous brown amps. The tone stack is designed to provide a wide and dynamic range of tonal options to the user. The Presence control works with the tone stack, and is designed to be a wide range control, effecting the overall sound of the entire circuit. The SOMA 63 features a steel core transformer in the audio signal path. The transformer lends to the overall tone shaping of the circuit, and when the gain is pushed hard, especially with higher output pickups, the small steel core transformer will saturate, just like a vintage amplifier. The SOMA 63 can be used as a tone-shaping preamp, or as an overdrive pedal. There are a wide variety of tones available in the SOMA 63, so spend some time with your new pedal, and find the tones that rock your world! The SOMA 63 runs off of a standard, negative center pin 9 volt power supply, and can be ran off of up to 18 volts. At 9 volts, the SOMA 63 will have more grit and texture. sources.bodyExcerpt: Soul Thrust Fuzz Unit by Greer Amps | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE Greer Amps Soul Thrust Fuzz Unit LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS FUZZ Description The Greer Amps Custom Shop SOUL THRUST FUZZ UNIT is an amazing sounding fuzz. This pedal is a two transistor fuzz pedal, utilizing NOS BC107B transistors. The Soul Thrust Fuzz Unit is built on a vintage style tag strip, with amplifier grade components, including 1 watt Carbon Film resistors, full size Bourns pots, and a mix of Panasonic ECQ and Mallory 150 type capacitors. This pedal features Volume and Frequency controls. The Frequency control allows for a wide range of tone. Fuzz is controlled by the guitar's volume control--want less fuzz? Roll your guitar volume down a bit, and the level of fuzz will decrease! This pedal sounds like a cross between a Germanium FF type fuzz, and a "Bender" type fuzz...mean and aggressive, this thing will kick out the meaty grind you're looking for! The Southland Harmonic Overdrive is built on the Lightspeed Organic Overdrive platform, we have developed what we believe to be the best overdrive on the market. The Lightspeed was built with the specific purpose of being a light to mild overdrive. The Southland is the next logical step for the Lightspeed platform—more gain, with two stages of clipping (utilizing different diode types for each stage of clipping), a focused midrange (not that annoying “hump”), and a bit of presence on top of the signal, to help cut through the mix. The Southland Harmonic Overdrive, like the Lightspeed, is touch sensitive, responds to pick attack, and has dynamics that just won’t stop. On top of that, we’ve selected a chip to drive the Southland that takes it to the next level. The Southland Harmonic Overdrive will fit with any musical style, and pairs amazingly well with the Lightspeed Organic Overdrive . The truth is that they don't. The revoicing of the circuit to have more of a focus on the mids, and more presence in the top end, as well as the increase in gain of the circuit, push the Southland to a place that the Lightspeed doesn't get to...one of the primary goals with the development of the Southland was to create a pedal that was different, AND would work well together with the Lightspeed. sources.bodyExcerpt: Greer Amps Sucker Punch Distortion - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Greer Amps Sucker Punch Distortion Posted By Pedal of the Day on Tuesday, June 23, 2015 in Greer Amps, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments --> --> I review a LOT of overdrive pedals. A LOT. While the majority of them sound awesome, once in a while I will plug one in and it blows me away right from the get-go, one that I immediately say to myself, “You have to find room for this on one of your pedalboards NOW.” One of these pedals is the Sucker Punch Distortion from Greer Amps, so let’s check it out! As soon as you unleash this thing onto your favorite amp of choice (tube-preferred, IMO), you will see what I’m talking about as far as tone and balls-out rock and roll are concerned. I felt like I was in the studio watching Slash and the boys record ‘ Appetite For Destruction ‘, except the tones from that great record were coming out of the amp in my practice space! Control-wise, there’s nothing revolutionary about the Sucker Punch. Volume, Gain and Tone are about as basic as it gets for a dirt pedal, but don’t let that fool you into thinking this is a one-trick pony, even thought it is a workhorse (hehe). The SP uses a JFET preamp to drive a 386D chip amp section, creating tones similar to early JCM amplifiers, some of the most coveted of the Marshall line. This stompbox is like having a Marshall in a box, with a huge amount of volume, great open and soaring amp-like tones and the crunch and meat of amp sounds heard on countless album recordings throughout the last 50 years. With a ton of range, great sounds and a really flamboyant yellow enclosure, the Sucker Punch is the complete package, without overdoing it or trying to cram too many unnecessary options into a perfect drive box. It’s not really a big surprise, as Nick and everyone at Greer Amps keep churning out great pedal after great pedal. This one really rocked my world, however, so cheers to you all in Georgia, and keep making this excellent gear for us all to enjoy! Specs: Face melting tone! JFET gain stage driving chip amp section! JCM-amp type distortion! Huge amount of volume on tap! Wide tone sweep, for thick or cutting settings! True Bypass! Uses 9Volt battery or standard neg. center, 2.1mm power supply. Current draw: 12mA. The Greer Amps Supa Cobra is a versatile and touch sensitive overdrive. The Supa Cobra offers the user incredible flexibility in a small form factor, with natural, amp like breakup and sensitivity. The 3 position toggle allows for flexibility in the clipping style and texture. When in FAT mode, the circuit clips in a fat, chewy way. When in LED mode, the clipping becomes stiffer (think of that famous British amp sound that starts with an M that is known for some crunchy textures), with more crunch--this setting is most noticeable at higher gain settings. When the clip switch is in the center position, the natural drive of the opamp is on display. The body control is a unique control to the Supa Cobra. When set low, the pedal remains cleaner, with less boom on the low notes. When the body control is increased, both gain and low-end presence are increased. The Supa Cobra runs off of a standard, negative center pin 9 volt power supply. Greer Amps’ lifetime warranty covers manufacturing defects and component failure to the original owner, it does not cover misuse or abuse. Current draw: 7mA. The Super Hornet has been a long time in the making…at least in Nick’s mind. Based on one very special FOXX Tone Machine in Nick’s collection, this pedal is a shop favorite when it comes to fuzz and anything octave. We took the basic building blocks of the vintage circuit, tweaked it, put a little bit of special sauce in the design by using NOS BC-107B transistors , and threw an added feature in the mix. You’ll notice that there is an octave toggle, like on the vintage units that these pedals are styled after…but, that’s not just a straight-forward on/off toggle. When the toggle is in STINGER mode, the momentary STINGER switch becomes active. You can simply stand on the momentary switch, to engage the OCTAVE for a lead run, then come off of the STINGER switch to return to normal fuzz, or even tap the switch, to flutter the octave on and off. This feature is absolutely awesome. When the toggle is in OCTAVE mode, the fuzz is permanently an OCTAVE fuzz, and the STINGER switch is NOT ACTIVE. The fuzz control goes from light fuzz with some clean, to raging wall of fuzz tones. The tone control is a wide sweep tone control. All in all, this pedal is a perfect addition to any guitar or BASS player’s tone arsenal. The OCTAVE even works in low fuzz settings! NOS BC-107B transistors! Based on a classic rock machine! Light fuzz to aggressive, wall of fuzz tones! STINGER switch that allows for momentary octave when the fuzz is engaged! True Bypass Uses a standard neg. center, 2.1mm power supply only! 5 year warranty to the original owner Share: FOLLOW US! We took the basic building blocks of the vin Add to cart SKU: : EQY937612159 Category: Pedals Description Shopping Reviews The Super Hornet has been a long time in the makingat least in Nicks mind. Based on one very special FOXX Tone Machine in Nicks collection, this pedal is a shop favorite when it comes to fuzz and anything octave. We took the basic building blocks of the vintage circuit, tweaked it, put a little bit of special sauce in the design by usingNOS BC-107B transistors, and threw an added feature in the mix. Youll notice that there is an octave toggle, like on the vintage units that these pedals are styled afterbut, thats not just a straight-forward on/off toggle. When the toggle is in STINGER mode, the momentary STINGER switch becomes active. You can simply stand on the momentary switch, to engage the OCTAVE for a lead run, then come off of the STINGER switch to return to normal fuzz, or even tap the switch, to flutter the octave on and off. This feature is absolutely awesome. When the toggle is in OCTAVE mode, the fuzz is permanently an OCTAVE fuzz, and the STINGER switch isNOT ACTIVE.The fuzz control goes from light fuzz with some clean, to raging wall of fuzz tones. The tone control is a wide sweep tone control. All in all, this pedal is a perfect addition to any guitar or BASS players tone arsenal. The OCTAVE even works in low fuzz settings! NOS BC-107B transistors! Based on a classic rock machine! Light fuzz to aggressive, wall of fuzz tones! STINGER switch that allows for momentary octave when the fuzz is engaged! sources.bodyExcerpt: Tone Smuggler — Greer Amps Buffer Pedal | PedalFilter | PedalFilter Skip to main content The guitar pedal database Search pedals The fastest, most visual guitar pedal database. All signal, no noise. About • Collections • Blog • Compare • Privacy Policy • Terms of Service • Submit a pedal • © 2026 PedalFilter Clear Compare ( 0 ) Back Home Greer Amps Tone Smuggler Back to results Greer Amps Tone Smuggler Buffer Boost Two-stage Class A JFET overdrive. Gain spans clean boost to fuzz-like distortion. The Tone Smuggler uses two stages of Class A JFET gain to produce beautiful texture, overdrive, and distortion. This gain-laden overdrive easily straddles the line from overdrive to distortion and even fuzz, sounding like an extension of your guitar and amp. Gain control takes you from clean to screaming distortion, almost fuzz-like. Tone sweeps from dark and slightly muffled (smooth and buttery) to brighter than normal amp settings. Volume allows a huge amount of boost. Sensitive to pick attack and volume control settings. Clean amps make it sound cleaner; easily overdriven amps make it more gnarly. Used on tour by Peter Stroud, Jay Gonzalez (Drive-By Truckers), and Alex Weeden (Miranda Lambert). Size: 2.63" wide, 4.75" long, 1.5" tall. 9V battery or standard neg center 2.1mm power supply. True bypass with lifetime warranty. sources.bodyExcerpt: Greer Amps Tone Smuggler Overdrive - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Greer Amps Tone Smuggler Overdrive Posted By Pedal of the Day on Monday, September 15, 2014 in Greer Amps, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments --> --> The first pedal I heard from Greer Amps was the Burning Goat Overdrive ; after that, I knew I had to hear more. Which brings us to this little black beauty: the Tone Smuggler. A jack-of-all-trades overdrive pedal, this guy will excite, perplex and complicate you and your guitar tone, and you wouldn’t want it any other way. Simple, 3-knob control design is great: sometimes, the less to think about, the better. Unfortunately, you’re gonna still have to use your brains on this guy, as there are a plethora of tonal options to be found within this small, well-built, tank-like enclosure. When I first turned it on, it felt like a nice, cleanish boost pedal, with the Gain setting around 9:00, and the Tone at about noon. A great little pick-me-up for my amp, it made the tones jump up a few notches and really sparkle, as a good boost should, and you can really push your amp just by cranking up the Volume knob, with the other controls backed off a bit. Once I started messing with the rest of the range in that Gain knob, though, it was ON. Clean boost to mild overdrive, to chunky, tube-y overdrive to almost a fuzz pedal, this box has got a big assortment of options to play with, and none that will leave you puzzled, dumbfounded or perplexed. You’ll just be more of a badass, is all, and so will your guitar and amp. You’ll be playing with some fine company if you pick up a Tone Smuggler and rock it with your rig (see the list below). Nick and the fine folks at Greer Amps are sending some more great pedals our way for review here in a short minute, so they’ll be much more on tap for you guys to check out in the coming months. While you’re waiting, go see their site, and what they have to offer, ’cause they are making some fantastic effects pedals (oh yeah, and their amplifiers aren’t too shabby, either!). Specs: 2 stages of Class A JFET gain! Tones ranging from clean boost to distortion, bordering on fuzz! Sounds like an extension of your current guitar and amp rig! Sensitive to pick attack and volume control settings! Clean amps tend to make this pedal sound cleaner, easily overdriven amps tend to make this pedal sound more gnarly! True Bypass! Uses 9Volt battery or standard neg. center, 2.1mm power supply. Built with top quality components. Lifetime Warranty to the original owner! Pedals are currently built to order, and ship within 1-2 weeks of the order being placed, and funds entering our account! Henretta Engineering browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Henretta Engineering H-Bomb Fuzz Published on November 27, 2016 Henretta Engineering fuzz pedal Information Henretta Engineering This is the first in a new line of pedals we're rolling out in 2016 - the H-Bomb Fuzz. It uses aspects of our Purple Octopus octave up and Bluebird fuzz pedals from our small square "no-knob" line. The H-Bomb Fuzz can be nasty and abrasive, but you can still play complex chords without it falling apart. The "fuzz" control adds sustain as you turn it clockwise. The "volume" control allows plenty of boost to push your amp into more saturation. The H-Bomb series of pedals feature twisted takes and useful combinations of the stock circuits found in the Henretta Engineering line of small no-knob set-and-forget pedals. Sporting a design that stays true to the simple utilitarian ideals that define the Henretta brand, the H-Bomb pedals come in a more standard pedal enclosure and format with (gasp) actual knobs on the outside. The H-Bomb Fuzz is a nasty, screaming fuzz that combines elements of the Henretta Engineering Bluebird fuzz and Purple Octopus circuits. The Bluebird provides rich harmonic content while the Purple Octopus provides upper octave harmonics, slightly gated attack, and just enough nuance to make it fun while still be musical. The result is a fuzz that will remind you of the classics but interact with your other pedals like a more modern boutique offering. Features: FUZZ: Don’t be fooled; the sound is pretty fuzzy with this rolled fully counter-clockwise. When you turn this control clockwise, the saturation and sustain increases, and the sound takes on a thinner character. At extreme settings, pick attack has a piercing high-register push to make solos jump out of the mix. sources.bodyExcerpt: Himmelstrutz Elektro Art FETTO Apache Home News Amps Pedals Custom Shop Download About Contact Himmelstrutz Elektro Art FETTO Apache: X-Power Overdrive AVAILABLE ON DEMAND BACKGROUND While ‍making ‍our ‍remarkable ‍ FETTO ‍LaRocca ‍for ‍sure ‍we ‍got ‍curious: ‍how ‍can ‍this ‍thing ‍both ‍sound ‍and ‍feel ‍so ‍good? ‍ ‍ FETTO ‍LaRocca ‍was ‍our ‍first ‍product ‍based ‍upon ‍tube ‍technology, ‍high ‍voltage, ‍400 ‍volts ‍ tube ‍technology ‍to ‍be ‍all clear. ‍And ‍yeah, ‍did we ‍already ‍know ‍tubes ‍could ‍sound ‍great ‍for ‍music/guitars, ‍otherwise ‍they ‍would ‍not ‍still ‍be ‍used ‍in ‍so ‍many ‍applications. Owner’s Manual Next Review… FETTO History Buy Now Non EU: $349 USD Buy Now EU: €349 EUR ($19 USD shipping fee added when checking out via PayPal) OK, ALL CLEAR! The question though in this case was: Why is FETTO LaRocca so punchy, so dynamic, so articulated, so “real” and why do not transistor/solid state solutions react/sound or feel anywhere close to tubes in about every case? May the main reason be that transistors mostly run at 2-10% of the voltage/power of where tubes sound as its best? Will this lead to solid state solutions (transistors/op amps etc) sound – and feel – is just 2-10% “as good”? Interesting question… LET THERE BE LIGHT THERE So let them modern transistors be treated the same way as old fashioned tubes were/are treated – same for all – let us give those plastic little parasites the same food as FETTO LaRocca craved to get good – let’s feed them baby transistors with 400 volts! Now the adventure started for real! WAS Some electric chocks & that holy smoke later, 6 months or whatsoever, this pioneering investigation was completed: FETTO Apache showed up and jumped out in front of us ready to roll… LIGHT ‍FETTO ‍Apache ‍is ‍an ‍all ‍solid ‍state ‍(no ‍tubes) ‍device ‍in ‍which ‍we ‍(Himmelstrutz) ‍can’t ‍hear ‍or ‍feel ‍the ‍tube(s) ‍aint ‍there. ‍Without ‍a ‍doubt ‍we ‍say ‍this ‍is ‍the ‍most ‍powerful, ‍punchy, ‍dynamic, ‍articulated ‍solid ‍state ‍guitar ‍overdrive ‍we ‍have yet ‍experienced – actually ‍also ‍tube ‍versions ‍included: ‍rhythmic, ‍light, ‍real! ‍ LET THERE BE GUITAR! If ‍you’re ‍still ‍wondering ‍what ‍we’re ‍talking ‍about, ‍have ‍yourself ‍a ‍look ‍at ‍the ‍print ‍of ‍this ‍gangsta ‍and ‍you ‍will ‍see ‍that ‍the ‍Himmelstrutz ‍logotype ‍(the ‍bird/ostrich) ‍has ‍a ‍more ‍proud, ‍a ‍more ‍serious ‍and ‍tougher ‍look ‍than ‍ever ‍before – should ‍we ‍say ‍more ‍female? – you ‍don’t ‍question ‍or ‍mess ‍with ‍this ‍girl! Controls: Drive: Overdrive/Distortion control Tone: Tone control (passive treble cut) More: Boost level control Volume: as loud as you'll ever need Mid*: mid character (passive/3 way toggle) Presence*: more/less higher frequencies (passive/3 way toggle) GIMME: Overdrive true bypass switching MORE: Boost true bypass switching Internal controls: Bass, Gain trimmers * Thanks to the Mid and Presence switches difficult amps (ala Fender) can also get Great distortion. Details: All original and handmade Himmelstrutz design. A further developed Fetto Nord cross-fertilized with the amazing Fetto Custom - Fetto Nord+ has identical toggle switch options as the Fetto Custom! sources.description: Experience the Himmelstrutz FUGAZI Junior, a compact pedal blending fuzz, distortion, and overdrive. Perfect for stacking with other Himmelstrutz pedals, especially the FUGAZI to create layered, expansive tones. Enjoy 25% off when you purchase both together.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Himmelstrutz Elektro Art FUGAZI Junior Fuzz Home News Amps Pedals Custom Shop Download About Contact Himmelstrutz Elektro Art FUGAZI Jr. – Compact Tone Powerhouse Fugazi Alu Box/Blackface Not Just Another Fuzz! Meet the Himmelstrutz FUGAZI Jr. – the continuing saga of the GRAMPS/ GRAMPS Plus – now as a compact powerhouse that packs a blend of fuzz, distortion, overdrive and boost. Whether you're after subtle boosts or rich, gritty textures, this pedal delivers a versatile range of tones in a small package Next Owner’s Manual Review… IN / OUT Input Input impedance : ~180 kΩ (true bypass / unbuffered) / ~1 MΩ (buffered) Output Output impedance : ~10 kΩ Power DC Input 9–18 V DC , low current draw (no internal battery). Optional adapter: 9–18 V DC , center-negative (BOSS-style, regulated). Push Switch GIMME Mechanical switching (true bypass or buffer*). * Slide switch below output jack selects True Bypass or Discrete JFET Class-A buffer. LED Indicator Status LED LED turns ON/OFF depending on switch state. LED colour is the colour of the day . Potentiometers FUG Squal / fuzz / dirt / distortion BOWL Tone control (bass ↔ treble) OUT Output level – as loud as you want. Or more. Internals * 1 × GAIN jumper 1 × MID trimmer 1 × BIAS trimmer * May vary depending on production day, version and serial number. Dimensions & Weight Size 111.6 × 61.6 × 50.0 mm (L/W/H) Weight ~160 g (0.35 lbs) Colour / Finish May vary depending on season. From Jun 2024: Stockholm White (RAL 9010) with grey / silver print or raw aluminium with black faceplate. FIRST TEST (with FUGAZI first version) FUGAZI Jr. In Company With Other Pedals Want to push your sound further? The FUGAZI Jr. stacks exceptionally well with other pedals — especially other Himmelstrutz designs . Whether you add overdrive, delay , reverb , or even more fuzz, it integrates smoothly and expands your tonal range without getting muddy or unstable. Ready to refine your tone? The Himmelstrutz FUGAZI Jr. is the compact fuzz/fuzztortion that delivers more than expected. Try it and hear how it can reshape your sound. Delivered with FUGAZI Jr. ► Sound, feel and look you have not experienced before – this is not in any way just another Big Muff or a Fuzz Face ► 1 x printed Owner’s Manual ► 1 x Warranty: The Himmelstrutz Elektro Art products includes a 1 year limited materials- and factory warranty (from delivery date). The warranty does not include batteries and consumables. Product service is free of charge during the warranty time. The warranty does not include errors due to product modifications, internal adjustments, disassembly, negligence/violence, incorrect power supply usage/incorrect connections or thunder.
